originality.rationale: The theorem is correct, but the decisive support-exponent inequality is a direct algebraic consequence of two divisibilities already established in the proof of Noppakaew--Pongsriiam Theorem 6. Their proof has \(L_S\mid C_T\), \(L_T\mid C_S\), and \(C_S<\prod_{S}p^{sb}\), \(C_T<\prod_Tq^{sb}\); multiplying these displayed inequalities gives exactly the claimed product obstruction. In the range \(a<sb\), the powerful-number corollary then follows immediately by observing that every unique-support exponent at least two contributes a positive exponent. Under the required implication/corollary standard, the assigned claim is therefore covered even though the 2023 paper did not isolate it as a named theorem.
